newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Argentine senator says he's barred from post.
newsitem.headline: Argentine senator says he's barred from post.

text.p: A leading Argentine opposition politician told the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) on Monday that manoeuvres by the ruling Peronist party had prevented him from taking up a seat in the country's Senate.

Horacio Massaccessi, Radical Party candidate in Argentina's last presidential election, told the IPU's Human Rights Committee that he had brought his complaint to them because he had exhausted all possibilities at home.

In a speech made available to reporters, he said he was asking the IPU to ask the Argentine Senate "to take the necessary measures to bring me into the body....and to condemn it for failing to recognise my fundamental rights".

Massaccessi said he was elected as senator from Rio Negro province, of which he is a former governor, in November 1995 by the local legislature, but his ratification had been delayed by a Senate commission where the Peronists are in the majority.
When the commission finally accepted that his election was legal in May this year, he declared, procedural manoeuvres by ruling party senators had still barred him from taking up his seat.
"It is clear that the will of the voters has been ignored and will continue to be until I am allowed to take my seat in the Chamber to which I have been legally elected," he told the IPU Committee.
"What we are dealing with is a case of illegal refusal to accept the mandate of the people."

There was no comment on his appeal from the IPU, which is to contact the Argentine legislature to seek its comment on his charges. The Geneva-based body, set up in 1894, groups legislatures around the world and part of its work is to defend parliamentarians subject to civil and human rights violations.
